# DoU Block Kit Builder

> A web tool for building Block Kit messages for DoU channels, previewing them with the same
> renderer real messages use, and copying the payload JSON. https://block-kit.chatic.io/

DoU (chatic) is a messenger. A webhook sender can deliver a structured message — an error report,
a deployment notice — as a title, dividers and a field table instead of one block of plain text.
The format is a subset of Slack Block Kit. This tool builds that payload; it does not send messages.

## Panes

- **Compose** — start from a template or stack blocks one by one. Drag to reorder.
- **Message** — drawn with the **same renderer** as a real DoU message. That is why the preview
  cannot drift from the real thing: there is one renderer (`libs/block-kit`), shared by three apps.
- **Payload** — the JSON the blocks compile to. Editable both ways, and copyable.

## Supported blocks (four)

| Block | What |
|---|---|
| `header` | One line of title. `plain_text` only, `level` 1–4 |
| `section` | A paragraph (`text`) or a two-column label/value grid (`fields[]`) |
| `divider` | A horizontal rule |
| `context` | A small grey line: source, version, author |

Other blocks (`image`, `actions`, `rich_text`, …) **do not break the message.** They show in place
as their raw JSON under an `UNSUPPORTED BLOCK` label. Leaving out `actions` (buttons) is deliberate:
DoU has no interactivity endpoint for a button press to go back to, so drawing one would be a lie.

## Text syntax — Slack mrkdwn

`*bold*` · `_italic_` · `~strike~` · `` `code` `` · ` ```code block``` ` · `<url|label>` ·
`<url>` · `<@U123>`. A delimiter inside a word is not read as a mark (`user_id` keeps its underscore).

**This is not the DoU composer's dialect.** The app's composer uses `**bold**` (two asterisks).
Put `**x**` in Block Kit text and it does not turn bold — the asterisks show as typed.

## Templates

Error · Attendance · Deployment.

## How the payload is used

The sender (`chatic-socials-api` / webhook) sends it. The client reads `chat.blocks$` first, then a
`{"blocks":[...]}` JSON body in `content`, then plain text. It does not look at `contentType`. The
reading rules live with the renderer, in `libs/block-kit` of the dou-app repository.
